why: Same theorem, two presentations. A (Hausdorff X) takes two maps h₁, h₂ : ℝⁿ → X, continuous and injective on the closed ball, whose images cover X, meet exactly in h₁(Sⁿ⁻¹), and have the same boundary sphere. B takes two closed subsets with homeomorphisms to the ball, a point of one lying in the other iff it maps to the unit sphere. Neither assumes more than the other. A ⇒ B: B does not assume X Hausdorff, but a space covered by two closed Hausdorff subspaces is Hausdorff (proved). Each homeomorphism is then extended to a map ℝⁿ → X. B ⇒ A: compact images in a Hausdorff space are closed, and an injective map continuous on the compact ball is a homeomorphism onto its image. The boundary conditions translate using injectivity. alexanderConeHomeomorph is a definition (vocabulary).
